title: Fixed-attempt retry with attempt cap
description: The operation is retried up to a fixed maximum number of attempts, then the failure is surfaced instead of looping forever. A cap bounds the worst-case cost of a retry storm. Callers distinguish retryable errors (timeouts, 503s) from permanent ones (400s, auth failures) before retrying. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers retrying up to N attempts, then surfacing the failure.

title: Exponential backoff with jitter
description: Waits between retries grow exponentially (1s, 2s, 4s, ...) so a struggling service gets breathing room. Random jitter is added to each wait so that many clients do not retry in lockstep and create a thundering herd. This combination is the industry standard for retry timing. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers computing exponential waits with a fixed base.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: {"base": 1.0, "n": 4}, 2: {"base": 0.5, "n": 6}, 3: {"base": 0.25, "n": 8}}
import random
random.seed(7)
base, n = CFG[LEVEL]["base"], CFG[LEVEL]["n"]
waits = []
for i in range(n):
    exp = min(base * (2 ** i), 30.0)          # exponential, capped
    waits.append(round(exp / 2 + random.random() * exp / 2, 3))  # equal jitter
print("waits:", waits)
print("monotonic growth check:", all(b >= a for a, b in zip([base] + waits, waits + [31])))

title: Retry budget
description: A retry budget caps the fraction of requests that may be retries within a time window, typically around 20 percent. When the budget is exhausted, further retries are denied even if attempts remain, which protects the system from retry-driven overload. Budgets are tracked per service and window. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers denying retries once the window budget is spent.
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Circuit breaker
description: A circuit breaker watches consecutive failures: after a threshold it opens and fails fast without calling the downstream, giving it time to recover. After a cooldown it enters half-open and lets one probe through; success closes the circuit, failure re-opens it. This stops cascading failures. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers opening the circuit after consecutive failures.
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Idempotent retry with request deduplication
description: Retries carry the same request identifier, and the server keeps a record of completed request ids. A retried request that the server already processed returns the cached result instead of executing twice. This makes retries safe for non-idempotent operations like charges and orders. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers returning cached results for duplicate request ids.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 2, 2: 3, 3: 4}
REPEATS = CFG[LEVEL]
completed, executions = {}, 0
def charge(req_id, amount):
    global executions
    if req_id in completed:
        return completed[req_id] + " (deduped)"
    executions += 1
    completed[req_id] = "charged $%d" % amount
    return completed[req_id]
out = [charge("req-1", 50) for _ in range(REPEATS)]
print("responses:", out)
print("actual executions:", executions, "(exactly-once)")
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.
